review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions of Positive.starMul (Model.lean), Positive.cut and its lemmas (Weights.lean), and squareCutMultiplier in CuntzIdentities.lean. I grepped the Analysis tree for existing projection simp lemmas on starMul, cut and abs, and found none in the JiangSu/TraceCone area. I also counted the call sites that unfold these definitions by hand. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simplifier behaviour. I did not recommend making `abs_val` simp, because a rule rewriting `(abs x).1` could pre-empt the existing @[simp] `abs_sq`. I did not recommend simp attributes on `squareCutMultiplier_zero` or `truncationMultiplier_zero`, because the identities are not clearly canonical simp normal forms. The bound-lemma proofs (`squareCutMultiplier_bound`, `starMul_add_le`) use `simpa only` or explicit simp sets, which is fine.

change cfcₙ (fun t => f t * f t) a.1 ≤
      ((δ : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ 2) • cfcₙ (fun t : ℝ => max (t - δ) 0) a.1
findings.problem: `Positive.cut` is a plain def with no simp or rw projection lemma for `(cut ε a).1`. Proofs therefore use `change` to restate the cfcₙ body by hand. The same hand-unfolding appears in many other files: Weights.lean (cut_le, norm_sub_cut_le), Cuntz.lean, RankCyclic.lean, FiniteCutComparison.lean, FiniteSpectralIntegral*Bounds.lean, CuntzRescaling.lean. These proofs depend on the exact form of the cut body, and the `change` statements are brittle when the definition changes.
findings.proposed_change: In Weights.lean, next to `Positive.cut`, add `@[simp] lemma cut_val (ε : ℝ≥0) (a : Positive A) : (cut ε a).1 = cfcₙ (fun t : ℝ => max (t - ε) 0) a.1 := rfl`. It has the shape of a `Subtype.val` of a constructor and cannot loop. Then `squareCut_factorization` can write `rw [Positive.cut_val, ← cfcₙ_mul f f a.1]` or use `simp only [Positive.cut_val]` instead of `change`. Other call sites can drop their `change` lines the same way.
findings.benefit: One canonical, discoverable unfolding rule replaces dozens of copied `change cfcₙ (fun t : ℝ => max (t-ε) 0) …` statements. `simp` can then normalise `(cut ε a).1` consistently when mixed with cfcₙ lemmas, and proofs no longer depend on how the cut body is spelled.

findings.declaration: Positive.starMul (no `.1` simp lemma; used via `simpa [Positive.starMul, …]` and `change` in abs_cuntzBelow_starMul, starMul_cuntzBelow_abs, abs_cut_cuntzBelow_of_norm_sub_lt)
findings.excerpt: exact ⟨g, by simpa [Positive.starMul, hgs, hg] using hη⟩
findings.problem: `Positive.starMul` has no projection lemma `(starMul x).1 = star x * x`. Callers unfold the whole definition with `simp [Positive.starMul, …]`, `dsimp [Positive.starMul]`, or `change ‖star g*(star y*y)*g - star (y*g)*(y*g)‖ < η` (line 140). The pattern recurs in this file (lines 58, 72, 140) and in about 20 other files. Unfolding the definition is not a stable simp interface. It exposes the Subtype structure, and `simp` may do more than the intended rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: In Model.lean, after `def starMul`, add `@[simp] lemma starMul_val (x : A) : (starMul x).1 = star x * x := rfl`. Likewise `mulStar_val : (mulStar x).1 = x * star x`. The right-hand side is strictly simpler, so there is no cycle. Then line 58 becomes `simpa [hgs, hg] using hη`, and the `change` at line 140 becomes `simp only [Positive.starMul_val]` or `show` is replaced by `rw [Positive.starMul_val]`. The `simp [Positive.starMul, …]` calls elsewhere can be replaced the same way.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical, targeted rewrite for `.1` of a starMul. They no longer unfold the definition, and the intent of each step is clearer. Proofs also keep working if `starMul`'s internal representation changes.

findings.excerpt: @[simp] lemma abs_sq (x : A) : (abs x).1 * (abs x).1 = star x * x :=
findings.problem: The only simp lemma for `Positive.abs` is `abs_sq`. It fires only on the product `(abs x).1 * (abs x).1`, and the file itself uses it through `rw` (lines 57, 69), not `simp`. There is no lemma for `(abs x).1` alone, and none for self-adjointness `star (abs x).1 = (abs x).1`. Proofs therefore restate the sqrt form by hand: `have hs := (CFC.sqrt_nonneg a.1).star_eq` at line 62, `change CFC.sqrt (star (x*q)*(x*q)) = c.1` at line 205, and `change … CFC.sqrt a.1 …` at line 72. Making `(abs x).1` simp-reducible to `CFC.sqrt …` would be risky, because it would pre-empt `abs_sq` and force sqrt rewriting everywhere. The interface is incomplete without such a lemma, but unconditionally unfolding is not the right fix.
findings.proposed_change: Add a non-simp unfolding lemma `abs_val (x : A) : (abs x).1 = CFC.sqrt (star x * x) := rfl`, to be used with `rw` or `simp only` where needed. Add `@[simp] lemma abs_star_eq (x : A) : star (abs x).1 = (abs x).1 := (CFC.sqrt_nonneg _).star_eq` (using `IsSelfAdjoint.star_eq`), so self-adjointness side goals close by `simp`. Then `change CFC.sqrt (…) = c.1` at line 205 becomes `rw [Positive.abs_val …]`, and `hs` at line 62 comes from the simp lemma.
findings.benefit: The three recurring facts about `abs` (unfolding, self-adjointness, square) become named lemmas. Downstream proofs, including the many other uses of `Positive.abs`, then use them directly and not through `change` on `CFC.sqrt`. Keeping the unfolding lemma non-simp avoids competing with `abs_sq`.
